questions.q: What causes the "small files problem" in a Delta table?
options: Frequent individual writes, like Lesson 22's UPDATE/MERGE operations or streaming micro-batches, each create their own small set of files over time
Delta tables always split data into exactly 1000 files regardless of write pattern
Reading a Delta table automatically fragments its files
It only happens if VACUUM has never been run
questions.explain: Reading many small files is genuinely slower than reading a few large ones, even at the same total data size.

options: Rewrites a table's small files into fewer, larger ones — same data, same schema, itself recorded as a Delta commit
Deletes old, unused data permanently
Changes the table's schema to a more efficient type
Only works on tables smaller than 1GB
questions.explain: New compacted files get added, old small ones get removed — exactly Lesson 17's add/remove mechanism, used for cleanup.

questions.q: What does ZORDER BY add on top of plain compaction?
options: It co-locates rows sharing similar values for the named column(s) within the compacted files, enabling file-level skipping on later filters
It sorts the entire table alphabetically by every column
It removes duplicate rows automatically
It converts the table back to plain Parquet
questions.explain: This is Foundations Lesson 61's partition pruning idea, but working at the level of individual files' contents.

questions.q: How often should OPTIMIZE typically be run?
options: As a periodic maintenance operation, scheduled to match how frequently the table receives writes — not after every single write
After every single write, without exception
Only once, when the table is first created
OPTIMIZE should never be scheduled as a job
questions.explain: A table with frequent small streaming writes needs it regularly; an infrequently-written table needs it rarely.

questions.q: Why does OPTIMIZE generate a new commit in the transaction log rather than modifying files silently?
options: It follows the same add/remove commit mechanism every other Delta write uses — nothing about it bypasses the log
OPTIMIZE is a read-only operation and doesn't touch the log at all
OPTIMIZE only works outside of Delta's transaction system
It doesn't generate a commit; the change is untracked
questions.explain: This keeps OPTIMIZE consistent with every guarantee ACID transactions (Lesson 18) provide.
